- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, true price often reverses or drops sharply; reduce forecast slope.
- After a sharp spike in model forecast, true price frequently overshoots then corrects — apply “overshoot correction” by reducing later forecast values by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often overcorrects downward — expect rebound; add 2–5% upward bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; true price often dips in first 5–7 days — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes, model tends to overreact — apply “sentiment dampening” by reducing forecast slope by 10–15%.
- Mean reversion observed in 30-day forecasts: if model is >90% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean.
